highlights.titleZh: Supermicro will sell SambaNova’s inference chips alongside Nvidia GPUs
highlights.content: Supermicro will build and sell AI inference systems that pair SambaNova’s SN50 chips with Nvidia GPUs, the companies said on Tuesday. The collaboration initially plans for 10,000 SN50 chips, according to SambaNova’s announcement. The racks will join Supermicro’s Data Center Building Block Solutions, the ready-made data centre systems it sells to customers. Running an AI model has two stages. First the system reads the prompt, then it writes the answer piece by piece. In the new racks, Nvidia GPUs do the reading and SN50 chips do the writing, SambaNova said. The company says AI agents work nonstop, so how fast they act depends on how fast the model responds. > “Agentic AI is the next wave of inference, and it has to run everywhere,” said Rodrigo Liang, co-founder and chief executive of SambaNova. “Now customers can order SN50 RDUs alongside GPUs, from a world-leading partner they trust.” ## Who does what Supermicro will put the systems together, test them, deliver them and support customers, including with on-site service. SambaNova engineers will get AI models running and tuned on SN50 and help with deployments. The companies will start with neoclouds, the cloud providers built for AI, and with sovereign clouds. Those keep data and computing inside one country. They then plan to sell to companies that run AI in their own data centres. > “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers,” said Charles Liang, president and chief executive of Supermicro. ## Built for existing data centres SN50 is SambaNova’s fifth-generation Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit, or RDU, a chip designed for inference. The company says it can serve the largest models without needing extreme power density in each rack. A SambaRack SN50 draws an average of 20 kW, SambaNova said last week. Operators can add inference capacity in data centres they already run, according to SambaNova. They do not have to wait for new builds held back by power and cooling. It says they can also keep using their existing GPUs for longer. The two companies say they can deliver much more inference capacity in 2027 as a result. ## SambaNova’s other recent deals The Supermicro deal follows another one with Oracle. Oracle said at its AI World conference on 27 October that it plans to deploy SN50 chips in its cloud data centres. It will offer the capacity to AI model builders. Two days later, SambaNova signed Emergys, a digital transformation services company, to deploy and run its platform for enterprise customers. SambaNova, founded in 2017 and based in San Jose, raised new funding at an $11 billion valuation in July. In June, Foxconn and Intel joined it to build rackscale AI infrastructure. ## Get the TNW newsletter Get the most important tech news in your inbox each week. ## Popular articles * 1 * 2 * 3 * 4 * 5

highlights.content: UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Google fine-tunes its Agentic Data Cloud to support highly scalable autonomous AI workers Artificial intelligence is no longer just about conversational assistants that tell people what to do. These days, it’s all about work automation, and Google Cloud is making sure it’s right at the forefront of that trend with its revamped Agentic Data Cloud platform, which received a host of new updates today. The Agentic Data Cloud was launched earlier this year at Google Cloud Next. It’s meant to be the architectural “system of action” for AI agents, replacing the brittle extract, transform and load-based data pipelines, or ETL, that feed legacy software applications. The key advantage of Agentic Data Cloud is that it meets customers where their data is, so rather than forcing them to squeeze all of their information in a large, centralized data warehouse, it enables AI agents to access it wherever it lives. In a blog post, Sirish Chandrasekaran, Google’s vice president of product management for data analytics, outlined the company’s belief that autonomous agents rather than humans will soon become the primary consumers of data. As such, it makes sense to build a purpose-built infrastructure stack specifically for them, prioritizing low latency, zero data movement and automated governance. “That is why we built the Agentic Data Cloud — a system of action designed to activate all your data by breaking down walled gardens, deliver high accuracy and trust, and operate proactively at low cost,” Chandrasekaran said. The flagship new feature in Agentic Data Cloud is borderless Lakehouse, a special version of Google’s “cross-border Lakehouse” product that also debuted at Cloud Next. Chandrasekaran said borderless Lakehouse is built upon the open-source Apache Iceberg table format and designed to eliminate multicloud friction with new caching capabilities for Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure. This allows companies to query remote data held in those cloud platforms over a secure private link, without having to pay egress fees. Chandrasekaran detailed how it works, saying that it automatically caches retrieved data blocks within Google Cloud to accelerate subsequent queries. There’s also a new AlloyDB integration that allows users to query external Iceberg tables with standard PostgreSQL queries without having to copy data. In this way, it bridges real-time transactional data with historical lakehouse records. ### More grounded agents One of the big problems with autonomous agents is that they can be prone to hallucinations without proper guardrails in place, which is why Google has overhauled another capability within Agentic Data Cloud. The Knowledge Catalog, which is a kind of map of business meaning that’s meant to inform AI agents of the peculiarities of the organization they work for, is getting a new self-learning enrichment capability in preview. According to Chandrasekaran, it works by continuously scanning unstructured data in Google Workspace, Jira, SharePoint and GitHub to translate operational knowledge into Open Knowledge Format context sets. These can be used to ground AI agents in organizational knowledge, and the results from early adopters shows that it can help make the average agent four-times more accurate, while reducing token consumption by up to 75%. Knowledge Catalog is seen as so important to Google’s agentic future that it’s also being enabled by default in the Gemini application starting today. Because it’s so tightly integrated, it can resolve issues around business metric definitions and access controls before it translates user’s prompts into Structured Query Language queries. Companies can also choose to ground agents in semantic models for specific data platforms, including Google BigQuery, Snowflake, SAP, Looker and dbt. “Agents are only as accurate as the business context they’re grounded in,” Chandrasekaran said. “Whether an agent is calculating net revenue for fi...

highlights.content: UPDATED 11:05 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Tencent releases Hy4, powerful frontier LLM introducing visual understanding and computer use by Kyt Dotson Tencent Holdings Ltd. today introduced Hy4, a new large language model that adds computer-use capabilities for the first time, using advanced visual understanding, reasoning and tool-calling to deliver long-horizon agentic performance. The company said the model marks a significant leap in performance over its Hy4 Preview, which arrived August 28, weighing in at 770 billion parameters with 49 billion active parameters. Both provide a 1 million token context window, putting it in the same range as current open-weights frontier models from European and Chinese developers, including Mistral AI SAS, Beijing Moonshot Technology Co. Ltd. and Z.AI Co. Ltd. The company said it substantially scaled both pre-training and post-training, reporting gains over the preview version in instruction following, long-context understanding, agentic long-horizon tasks, and deep research. Tencent also identified excessive reasoning and over-verification during the previous version’s “thinking” processes. The new model focuses heavily on real-world productivity for workplace collaboration, human experience and professional work. The company said it optimized long-context learning capabilities to understand complex information, including web development, document summarization, visual creative tasks, document presentation, and more. The company added that it also enhanced its capability for front-end and game development, high-complexity tasks that include intricate business logic, state management, and orchestration. Some models struggle with producing stateful, elegant and beautiful user interfaces that are visually polished and also fully functional. It is not uncommon for professional game developers, industry engineers and amateur vibe coders to use AI models as part of their work. However, a recent spate has had coders begin to reproduce, reverse engineer and clone older and semi-recent video games. This caused Anthropic PBC to block Claude Code and its underlying Opus 5.5 model from assisting in these tasks. The company said it integrated deeply with major engines such as Unreal Engine, Unity, and Godot, giving it the capability to support complex game logic and multiplayer implementations. Compared to the preview, Tencent said Hy4 improved by 19.1 percent in the GameDev bench and 9.8 percent in GameLogic benchmarks, although the actual baseline numbers remain internal and weren’t released. To advance scientific reasoning, Tencent advanced the next stage of Recursive Self-Improvement to enhance research and development capabilities. Using the Hyra 2.0 harness, an autonomous AI research agent system, the model optimized the pre-training infrastructure for smaller models sharing the same architecture. The model is currently available on Tencent Cloud TokenHub, WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy, Yuanbao, WeCom’s AI Assistant, Ima and more. It can also be accessed via third-party sources such as OpenRouter, Hermes and OpenCode. The company added that, despite its significant enhancements over Hy4 Preview, it kept costs low, maintaining the same pricing at around $0.90 per million input tokens, $2.70 per million output tokens, and $0.045 per million cached input tokens. highlights.content: UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Exclusive: BlueFlag Security expands AI agent governance to cover unapproved coding agents by Duncan Riley Software development security startup BlueFlag Security Inc. today expanded the artificial intelligence agent governance tools in its developer risk platform to cover unapproved coding agents, including those running on engineers’ laptops outside the code repository. The update also brings automated fixes for some of the risks the platform turns up. BlueFlag is going after a problem that has grown fast as coding assistants have evolved into agents that plan their own work and spin up the environments they need. Many sign in with a developer’s credentials. An agent working that way inherits every permission the developer holds. Raj Mallempati, BlueFlag’s co-founder and chief executive, described the AI agent as “the most powerful and least governed identity in the development environment.” The company plans to start interrupting attack paths as they form early next year, he said. For now, the platform reports them. In the current release, the work starts with finding the agents, which BlueFlag does from activity in the code. It picks up each agent through the commits and pull requests it produces, then classifies it by what it does with the code and whose identity it uses. Security teams can trace any agent back to the developers who work with it and the repositories it operates in, with unapproved agents marked as such. AI tools running locally on a developer’s machine are harder to spot. To catch those, BlueFlag reads data from endpoint detection and response products such as those from CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. and SentinelOne Inc., so nothing new has to be installed on the device. Human review gets its own checks. BlueFlag now flags pull requests approved by an AI agent, along with commits an agent wrote from start to finish and pipeline runs that went out with no person signing off. Organizations can also require a human review before anything merges or deploys. For any software release, customers can document where a person was in the decision and where one was not. A separate inventory looks at AI inside the applications a company builds. It records the model providers and agent frameworks each application relies on and scores them against the Open Worldwide Application Security Project’s Top 10 for Agentic Applications. AI spending is measured as well. BlueFlag ties the tokens and dollars each developer burns through to the commits and accepted code that came out of them, and it points to places where spending keeps climbing with no new commits behind it. Paid seats that sit idle show up in the same report. Remediation runs through two new tools. AccessGuard targets identity problems such as overpermissioned accounts and stale credentials. Misconfigured repositories and pipelines are handled by DriftGuard, which corrects settings such as missing branch protections that drift over time. Fixes can be applied by hand from written instructions or run automatically with one click, and automated changes can be rolled back. Auto parts supplier Marelli Holdings Co. Ltd. is a customer. Kristie Pfosi, its global chief information security officer, said agentic AI made the unknowns inside her company’s own development environment bigger “overnight.” “Within the first week BlueFlag showed us which AI agents were working in our repositories, which developers they worked with, and where the gaps were in how they were approved, scoped and reviewed,” Pfosi said. “Those are findings we can act on the same day.” The launch comes a day after BlueFlag published its first research report, “The State of Developer Risk 2026.” Its figures come from metadata the platform collected on tens of thousands of identities and access tokens at a subset of BlueFlag’s enterprise customers, in a snapshot taken in September. AI Agents.content: UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Google fine-tunes its Agentic Data Cloud to support highly scalable autonomous AI workers Artificial intelligence is no longer just about conversational assistants that tell people what to do. These days, it’s all about work automation, and Google Cloud is making sure it’s right at the forefront of that trend with its revamped Agentic Data Cloud platform, which received a host of new updates today. The Agentic Data Cloud was launched earlier this year at Google Cloud Next. It’s meant to be the architectural “system of action” for AI agents, replacing the brittle extract, transform and load-based data pipelines, or ETL, that feed legacy software applications. The key advantage of Agentic Data Cloud is that it meets customers where their data is, so rather than forcing them to squeeze all of their information in a large, centralized data warehouse, it enables AI agents to access it wherever it lives. In a blog post, Sirish Chandrasekaran, Google’s vice president of product management for data analytics, outlined the company’s belief that autonomous agents rather than humans will soon become the primary consumers of data. As such, it makes sense to build a purpose-built infrastructure stack specifically for them, prioritizing low latency, zero data movement and automated governance. “That is why we built the Agentic Data Cloud — a system of action designed to activate all your data by breaking down walled gardens, deliver high accuracy and trust, and operate proactively at low cost,” Chandrasekaran said. The flagship new feature in Agentic Data Cloud is borderless Lakehouse, a special version of Google’s “cross-border Lakehouse” product that also debuted at Cloud Next. Chandrasekaran said borderless Lakehouse is built upon the open-source Apache Iceberg table format and designed to eliminate multicloud friction with new caching capabilities for Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure. This allows companies to query remote data held in those cloud platforms over a secure private link, without having to pay egress fees. Chandrasekaran detailed how it works, saying that it automatically caches retrieved data blocks within Google Cloud to accelerate subsequent queries. There’s also a new AlloyDB integration that allows users to query external Iceberg tables with standard PostgreSQL queries without having to copy data. In this way, it bridges real-time transactional data with historical lakehouse records. ### More grounded agents One of the big problems with autonomous agents is that they can be prone to hallucinations without proper guardrails in place, which is why Google has overhauled another capability within Agentic Data Cloud. The Knowledge Catalog, which is a kind of map of business meaning that’s meant to inform AI agents of the peculiarities of the organization they work for, is getting a new self-learning enrichment capability in preview. According to Chandrasekaran, it works by continuously scanning unstructured data in Google Workspace, Jira, SharePoint and GitHub to translate operational knowledge into Open Knowledge Format context sets. These can be used to ground AI agents in organizational knowledge, and the results from early adopters shows that it can help make the average agent four-times more accurate, while reducing token consumption by up to 75%. Knowledge Catalog is seen as so important to Google’s agentic future that it’s also being enabled by default in the Gemini application starting today. Because it’s so tightly integrated, it can resolve issues around business metric definitions and access controls before it translates user’s prompts into Structured Query Language queries. AI Agents.content: UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Exclusive: BlueFlag Security expands AI agent governance to cover unapproved coding agents by Duncan Riley Software development security startup BlueFlag Security Inc. today expanded the artificial intelligence agent governance tools in its developer risk platform to cover unapproved coding agents, including those running on engineers’ laptops outside the code repository. The update also brings automated fixes for some of the risks the platform turns up. BlueFlag is going after a problem that has grown fast as coding assistants have evolved into agents that plan their own work and spin up the environments they need. Many sign in with a developer’s credentials. An agent working that way inherits every permission the developer holds. Raj Mallempati, BlueFlag’s co-founder and chief executive, described the AI agent as “the most powerful and least governed identity in the development environment.” The company plans to start interrupting attack paths as they form early next year, he said. For now, the platform reports them. In the current release, the work starts with finding the agents, which BlueFlag does from activity in the code. It picks up each agent through the commits and pull requests it produces, then classifies it by what it does with the code and whose identity it uses. Security teams can trace any agent back to the developers who work with it and the repositories it operates in, with unapproved agents marked as such. AI tools running locally on a developer’s machine are harder to spot. To catch those, BlueFlag reads data from endpoint detection and response products such as those from CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. and SentinelOne Inc., so nothing new has to be installed on the device. Human review gets its own checks. BlueFlag now flags pull requests approved by an AI agent, along with commits an agent wrote from start to finish and pipeline runs that went out with no person signing off. Organizations can also require a human review before anything merges or deploys. For any software release, customers can document where a person was in the decision and where one was not. A separate inventory looks at AI inside the applications a company builds. It records the model providers and agent frameworks each application relies on and scores them against the Open Worldwide Application Security Project’s Top 10 for Agentic Applications. AI spending is measured as well. BlueFlag ties the tokens and dollars each developer burns through to the commits and accepted code that came out of them, and it points to places where spending keeps climbing with no new commits behind it. Paid seats that sit idle show up in the same report. Remediation runs through two new tools. AccessGuard targets identity problems such as overpermissioned accounts and stale credentials. Misconfigured repositories and pipelines are handled by DriftGuard, which corrects settings such as missing branch protections that drift over time. Fixes can be applied by hand from written instructions or run automatically with one click, and automated changes can be rolled back. Auto parts supplier Marelli Holdings Co. Ltd. is a customer. Kristie Pfosi, its global chief information security officer, said agentic AI made the unknowns inside her company’s own development environment bigger “overnight.” “Within the first week BlueFlag showed us which AI agents were working in our repositories, which developers they worked with, and where the gaps were in how they were approved, scoped and reviewed,” Pfosi said. “Those are findings we can act on the same day.” The launch comes a day after BlueFlag published its first research report, “The State of Developer Risk 2026.” Its figures come from metadata the platform collected on tens of thousands of identities and access tokens at a subset of BlueFlag’s enterprise customers, in a snapshot taken in September. [SAPs](/themen/SAPs), [Agent](/themen/Agent) # SAP's AI Agent Push Spans Development, Partner Networks and Sovereign Infrastructure Published on 11/04/2026 at 16:31 | Editorial boerse-global.de SAP unveiled AI agent tools and an NTT sovereignty tie-up at TechEd; investors now weigh whether they add to 26% cloud revenue growth. ![SAPs, Agent, Push, Spans, Development, Partner, Networks, Sovereign, Infrastructure, SAP Illustration mit AI erstellt.](https://mdb.ad-hoc-news.de/bild/bild-2671060_1200_0.webp) SAPs, Agent, Push, Spans, Development, Partner, Networks, Sovereign, Infrastructure, SAP Illustration mit AI erstellt. SAP used this year's TechEd to widen its artificial intelligence footprint on several fronts at once, unveiling tools for building and managing AI agents while extending the technology into cross-company business processes. The announcements, made on 27 and 28 October, give investors a fresh set of questions to weigh: whether the expanded toolkit can add momentum to a cloud business that is already expanding briskly, or whether it amounts to technical showmanship that has yet to translate into revenue. The stock gained 3.4% on the day of the main presentation. Reading that move as a direct verdict on the product news would be a stretch — what matters for any forward-looking valuation is whether the new capabilities generate incremental demand. ## From building agents to deploying them At the center of the rollout is Joule Studio, alongside Joule Work and the SAP Business AI Platform. Together they provide the means to develop and govern AI agents, which the company frames under the "Autonomous Enterprise" concept. The scope therefore reaches beyond individual applications to the way those applications are created and controlled — a potential growth avenue, provided customers put the tools to productive use. A separate strand targets the spaces where trading partners interact. SAP announced agentic AI capabilities for its Business Networks, aimed at smoothing collaboration and operational workflows between companies. This is a distinct building block from the development tooling: one describes where agents are meant to operate, the other how they are made. Neither, on its own, constitutes evidence of commercial success. [Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying SAP?](https://www.stockstoday.com/lp/analysis/?trk=ST_Asset_Analysis_Middle_RSS-Feed&isin=DE0007164600&aktienname=SAP&adref=Blog_Ad-Hoc-News%3AEx-Article-ID_240538%3AISIN_DE0007164600%3AAsset_SAP%3ASource_Ad-Hoc-News&source=RSS-Ad-Hoc-News&Language=English) There is also a live deployment to point to. Four migration and modernization assistants are already supporting cloud-ERP transformations at early-adopter customers — a step beyond a pure announcement, though hardly proof of broad adoption. ## The cloud trajectory is the yardstick Underpinning all of it is the cloud franchise, which remains the decisive measure of whether the AI initiatives pay off. In third-quarter 2026 results reported roughly two weeks ago, SAP posted a 26% rise in cloud revenue, while the current cloud backlog reached €24.1 billion, up 26% at constant currencies. Those figures are the baseline against which the new tools should be judged. They are not, however, a validation of products unveiled afterward — investors would do well to separate existing demand from any additional impulse the AI features might create. The bull case rests on connecting product utility to the cloud offering. Should customers adopt the agent-building and management tools, SAP's portfolio could become more attractive — co...

AI Agents.content: [![openPR Logo](/fx/openpr-logo-slogan.svg)](/) * [PR-Wiki](/wiki/) * [Imprint](/news/imprint.html) [![openPR.com](/fx/flagge-uk.svg)](https://www.openpr.com/) [![openPR.de](/fx/flagge-de.svg)](https://www.openpr.de/) [![openPR Logo](/fx/openpr-logo-slogan.svg "openPR")](https://www.openpr.com/ "openPR") Press release # AI Agent Security Market to Reach USD 370.93 Billion by 2034, Growing at 39.49% CAGR 11-04-2026 12:08 PM CET | [IT, New Media & Software](/news/categories2-1-IT-New-Media-Software.html) ## Press release from: [Polaris Market Research & Consulting, Inc.](/news/archive/297361/Polaris-Market-Research-Consulting-Inc.html "archive und pressrelease of Polaris Market Research & Consulting, Inc.") [![AI Agent Security Market](https://cdn.open-pr.com/L/b/Lb04428549_g.jpg)](https://cdn.open-pr.com/L/b/Lb04428549_g.jpg "AI Agent Security Market") AI Agent Security Market The global AI agent security market is expected to reach USD 370.93 billion by 2034, registering a CAGR of 39.49% from 2026 to 2034, according to a new study by Polaris Market Research & Consulting, Inc. Growth is being driven by enterprises deploying autonomous agents that can access applications, tools, data and business processes on their own. Why AI Agents Need Their Own Security Layer Traditional AI security focused on protecting models and the data used to train them. Autonomous AI agents change the problem. An agent behaves like a software identity: it receives permissions, calls tools, chains actions across systems and can act without a human approving each step. That raises new questions for security teams. Which agent is acting? What is it allowed to touch? Can its actions be audited and reversed? Agentic AI security answers those questions through agent identity and lifecycle management, authorization, runtime protection, monitoring and audit trails. The report finds that agent identity and access security was the largest capability segment in 2025, with a 24.36% revenue share, because agents need controlled identities and permissions before they can operate safely. Get a free sample of the AI Agent Security Market report https://www.polarismarketresearch.com/industry-analysis/ai-agent-security-market#utm\_source=open+pr&utm\_medium=paid&utm\_campaign=open+pr&utm\_id=01 Five Signals Security Leaders Should Watch • Standards are forming. The National Institute of Standards and Technology launched its AI Agent Standards Initiative in February 2026, covering industry standards, Model Context Protocol (MCP) security and agent identity research. A related NCCoE concept paper addresses identification, authorization, auditing and non-repudiation. • Identity vendors are consolidating. Okta acquired Permiso Security for USD 200 million, Cyera acquired Oasis Security for USD 1 billion, and Palo Alto Networks acquired CyberArk for about USD 25 billion. • Dedicated products are launching. Okta released Okta for AI Agents and Ping Identity introduced Identity for AI, while Zenity, Obsidian Security, Oligo Security and GitGuardian raised funding for agent governance and non-human identity security. • MCP is a new attack surface. As MCP adoption grows across enterprise AI stacks, demand is rising for protocol security and agent-to-tool controls. • Cloud leads deployment. Cloud-based solutions held a 61.36% share in 2025, reflecting the shift of applications, APIs and identity platforms to the cloud. "Autonomous agents are creating a new security layer built around agent identity, permissions and controlled execution. Standards work, enterprise adoption and specialist investment are together forming a dedicated AI agent security category," said a Senior Artificial Intelligence Analyst at Polaris Market Research. Where Agentic AI Security Fits in the Wider Stack AI agent security sits alongside, but is distinct from, broader AI in cybersecurity tools that use machine learning to detect threats. Leidos ([![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/leidos-holdings.svg)LDOS](/symbols/NYSE-LDOS/)) is addressing that need with **HeadWay Dispatch™**, a new platform that gives organizations [three ways to govern AI agents](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4813679-1&h=3167261392&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.leidos.com%2Finsights%2Fknow-control-prove-building-trust-agentic-ai&a=three+ways+to+govern+AI+agents): ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/leidos-holdings.svg) **What it provides** **Key perspective:** "HeadWay Dispatch is designed to give organizations oversight without requiring them to start over with their existing AI investments," said Steve Hull, president of Leidos Digital. "As AI agents operate with greater autonomy, organizations need to know when to trust them, when to intervene and how to account for their actions." **What's next:** Leidos is developing two additional HeadWay Dispatch capabilities: Experience, which will tailor what each operator sees based on their role and mission needs, and Intelligence, which will coordinate AI agents from different vendors under a common policy. Leidos is also extending HeadWay Dispatch so its controls hold when network connections are degraded or lost. **Go deeper:** **About HeadWay™**HeadWay Dispatch is a part of the HeadWay™ product suite. HeadWay integrates enterprise data platforms, advanced analytics and AI to deliver continuous operational insight and make informed decisions. Now organizations can put AI agents to work that understand the business, operate within its controls, and can be trusted to deliver real results. These product advancements include [**Business Ontology**](http://snowflake.com/en/blog/real-time-analytics-snowflake/),4 which grounds agents in definitions the business has approved, while [**Cortex AI Gateway**](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/features/cortex-ai-gateway/)2 governs every model, tool, and action those agents touch. With that foundation in place, [**Snowflake CoCo**](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/snowflake-coco/), the coding agent for data teams, and [**Snowflake CoWork,**](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/snowflake-cowork/) the personal work agent for knowledge workers, take on the recurring work that slows teams down across the business to drive impact. Pushing autonomous work even further, new **CoCo and CoWork Bots**5 serve as always-on AI coworkers that continuously work in the background, act directly in the tools teams already use, and check in only when a decision or sign-off is required. Most enterprises don’t have trouble building an AI agent. They have trouble trusting one enough to put it into production. According to a recent MIT Technology Review [report](https://www.snowflake.com/en/lp/raising-the-quality-of-insights-in-agentic-analytics/) sponsored by Snowflake, 55% of executives cite a lack of business context as the primary cause of low-quality AI agent insights, with fragmented or inaccessible data ranking second at 45%. An agent that doesn’t know how the company defines revenue gives a confident wrong answer that someone has to catch. Meanwhile, agents are connecting to models, MCP servers, and enterprise systems faster than IT and security can keep up, which brings new risks and unexpected bills. As a result, a lot of companies are keeping their AI agents in pilot phase, grappling with how to fully trust and control these agents in order to scale them across the business. Snowflake is uniquely positioned to close that gap. For over 14,500 global enterprises,1 Snowflake already sits at the center of the data, business context, AI models, and workflows that agents depend on, serving as the governed control plane for the agentic enterprise. Today’s announcements turn that foundation into a complete system for the agentic enterprise. Context, controls, and execution are built together, so each makes the others stronger. “The enterprises that win won’t be the ones with the most agents. LLMs.titleZh: Tencent releases Hy4, powerful frontier LLM introducing visual understanding and computer use - SiliconANGLE
LLMs.content: UPDATED 11:05 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Tencent releases Hy4, powerful frontier LLM introducing visual understanding and computer use by Kyt Dotson Tencent Holdings Ltd. today introduced Hy4, a new large language model that adds computer-use capabilities for the first time, using advanced visual understanding, reasoning and tool-calling to deliver long-horizon agentic performance. The company said the model marks a significant leap in performance over its Hy4 Preview, which arrived August 28, weighing in at 770 billion parameters with 49 billion active parameters. Both provide a 1 million token context window, putting it in the same range as current open-weights frontier models from European and Chinese developers, including Mistral AI SAS, Beijing Moonshot Technology Co. Ltd. and Z.AI Co. Ltd. The company said it substantially scaled both pre-training and post-training, reporting gains over the preview version in instruction following, long-context understanding, agentic long-horizon tasks, and deep research. Tencent also identified excessive reasoning and over-verification during the previous version’s “thinking” processes. The new model focuses heavily on real-world productivity for workplace collaboration, human experience and professional work. The company said it optimized long-context learning capabilities to understand complex information, including web development, document summarization, visual creative tasks, document presentation, and more. The company added that it also enhanced its capability for front-end and game development, high-complexity tasks that include intricate business logic, state management, and orchestration. Some models struggle with producing stateful, elegant and beautiful user interfaces that are visually polished and also fully functional. It is not uncommon for professional game developers, industry engineers and amateur vibe coders to use AI models as part of their work. However, a recent spate has had coders begin to reproduce, reverse engineer and clone older and semi-recent video games. This caused Anthropic PBC to block Claude Code and its underlying Opus 5.5 model from assisting in these tasks. The company said it integrated deeply with major engines such as Unreal Engine, Unity, and Godot, giving it the capability to support complex game logic and multiplayer implementations. Compared to the preview, Tencent said Hy4 improved by 19.1 percent in the GameDev bench and 9.8 percent in GameLogic benchmarks, although the actual baseline numbers remain internal and weren’t released. To advance scientific reasoning, Tencent advanced the next stage of Recursive Self-Improvement to enhance research and development capabilities. Using the Hyra 2.0 harness, an autonomous AI research agent system, the model optimized the pre-training infrastructure for smaller models sharing the same architecture. The model is currently available on Tencent Cloud TokenHub, WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy, Yuanbao, WeCom’s AI Assistant, Ima and more. It can also be accessed via third-party sources such as OpenRouter, Hermes and OpenCode. The company added that, despite its significant enhancements over Hy4 Preview, it kept costs low, maintaining the same pricing at around $0.90 per million input tokens, $2.70 per million output tokens, and $0.045 per million cached input tokens. The Flash version of the model is scheduled for release soon to deliver greater cost efficiency for users. The company also said it intends to release the model weights and system cards in the coming days as part of its commitment to responsible open-source AI development. ##### Image: Tencent # A message from John Furrier, co-founder of SiliconANGLE: Support our mission to keep content open and free by engaging with theCUBE community. Get trending papers in your email inbox! # Daily Papers ## by[AK](/akhaliq) and the research community ![](/front/assets/papers-by.png) ### [EvoUndo: Recoverability-Constrained Self-Evolution for LLM Agent Harnesses](/papers/2608.28363) LLM agents increasingly modify their own prompts, tools, middleware, resources, and execution harnesses at runtime. Such self-evolution can improve capability, but a successful mutation may leave persistent effects that cannot be safely reversed in states different from the one in which it was created. We introduce EvoUndo, a framework for representing, synthesizing, diagnosing, and independently verifying recoverability of model-generated self-modifications across counterfactual states. Across 600 unseen one-shot self-evolution tasks, we identify 197 capability-improving mutations that fail recoverability verification. Under the original recovery representation, conventional repair strategies recover 0/197 of these natural failures. Deterministic oracle analysis recovers 48/197 under the original recovery language L0, while the extended recovery calculus increases empirical oracle recovery to 191/197. A protocol-locked 2x2 grounding-by-expressivity intervention then separates two bottlenecks: exact state-address grounding increases successful recovery from 0/48 to 38/48 (79.2%) when the original language is sufficient, while extending the recovery language enables recovery on 142/143 (99.3%) failures in the oracle-defined S1 stratum. On the primary gpt-oss-120b backbone, adding exact-address diagnostics to the richer language reduces recovery to 133/143 (93.0%); a Qwen3.8-27B replication preserves the grounding and expressivity effects but not this negative interaction, indicating that the latter is model-dependent. These results indicate that reliable agent self-evolution requires co-designing verification, state grounding, witness semantics, and recovery-language expressivity rather than relying on iterative prompting alone. ![](https://cdn-avatars.huggingface.co/v1/production/uploads/65720df8e724eeab558d5b25/R_iFiRVK4vAmtbZ5Wo1aJ.jpeg) ![](/avatars/df7b0cd45f0be774c3160fe27efdf91b.svg) ![](https://cdn-avatars.huggingface.co/v1/production/uploads/64de9c210f599f78efa3c7d4/LJN_iUNVuv6IHn3nebhcn.jpeg) ### [FACTWASH: Catching AI Rewrites That Wash Hearsay into Fact](/papers/2608.03372) AI systems rewrite information constantly: conversations become stored memories, documents become answers. The rewrite can keep a claim while washing away what made it checkable, who said it, how sure they were, when it held. We call that failure factwashing, and release factwash, an open-source write-time gate that catches it deterministically, with named flags and evidence rather than an LLM judge. Building it answers a practical question: when does a cheap check suffice, and when do you need a model? What decides is whether the property has a bounded surface-cue inventory. Explicit negation cues are close to enumerable, so a word list finishes and transfers, reaching 0.91 F1 on untuned text. Hedging and attribution have open-ended realizations, so vocabulary plateaus near half recall, and a one-question LLM witness recovers +17 and +15 points of cue-detection recall at equal precision. Deployed, that witness may only lower a verdict, so it buys precision rather than coverage. We measure cue detection on 105,596 independently annotated sentences. A blind-labelled corpus of memory writes then locates the failure: 55% of bad writes in conversational hearsay, 7% in business email (p < 0.001), so the first deployment question is not which detector to use but whether the failure occurs at all. On unmodified mem0 2.0.7, the gate flags 5 of 8 hedged-hearsay writes. ### [What Does an Evaluation License? Learn how to cut AI spend and build faster in your startup. ![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/b8764cf70d22d850d0d6830dbc4ef0fc4a4218b9418ea6b20f267d45c909454a?s=48&d=mm&r=g) [Violetta Bonenkamp](https://blog.mean.ceo/author/team/) ## TL;DR: Latest AI Developments News, November 2026, and What Founders Should Do Now Table of Contents [Toggle](#) The latest AI developments news for November 2026 shows you a split market. Top-tier AI gets pricier, while open models and cheaper chips bring near-frontier power to solo founders and small teams. • **Coding speed jumped.** Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 programmed a robodog 20x faster than last year's best human team. Your hardware or IoT prototypes can now ship in weeks instead of months. • **Costs move in two directions.** Nvidia's memory costs rose 485%, and one of its latest systems costs about $7.8 million to build. A 1.6 trillion parameter open model trained without Nvidia chips and a 100x energy cut point to cheaper compute ahead. Use small models for routine work and frontier models for hard reasoning. For more on vendor pricing, read these [AI cost signals from August 2026](https://blog.mean.ceo/latest-ai-developments-news-august-2026). • **Voice and chat are merging.** SoundHound AI's purchase of LivePerson targets a $500 million cross-selling opportunity. Single-channel tools face pressure, and vertical depth in healthcare or finance protects your pricing. • **AI is leaving the browser.** Claude in Lucyd smart glasses and voice-based monitoring tools open markets in trades, care and field work. They also bring GDPR risks. • **Humans stay in charge.** Studies on therapy bots and on an AI that "knew the answers but didn't understand the questions" carry one lesson. Keep a person accountable for any output touching health, money or legal matters. LLMs.content: * Featured * [Corporate](https://www.tencent.com/category/corporate/) * [For business](https://www.tencent.com/topic/topic-for-business/) * [For consumers](https://www.tencent.com/topic/topic-for-consumers/) * [Innovation](https://www.tencent.com/topic/topic-innovation/) # Tencent Launches Hy4, Joining the Ranks of the World’s Leading Open-Source AI Models November 4, 2026 Tencent today announced the release of Tencent Hy4, its latest-generation large language model, marking a significant leap in performance and capabilities that now ranks it among the world’s leading open-source AI models. Tencent Hy plans to release model weights and system cards in the coming days, reinforcing its commitment to responsible open-source AI development, with a focus on cybersecurity and biological safety. The new model also introduces visual understanding capabilities for the first time, alongside major improvements in instruction following, long-context comprehension and long-horizon agentic tasks, delivering stronger overall performance across a diverse set of applications. Through advanced visual understanding, reasoning, and tool-calling capabilities, Hy4 now supports a broader range of tasks, including fine-grained image processing, complex chart analysis, and mathematical visual reasoning. Additionally, Hy4 introduces computer-use capabilities for the first time, enabling it to interact with both command-line interfaces and graphical user interfaces to perform a wide range of work and everyday tasks. The model has undergone specialized training on professional software such as Blender and CAD, significantly enhancing its ability to plan and execute long-horizon and sophisticated tasks. #### Deep Model-Product Co-Design Unlocks New Opportunities for Real-World Productivity Leveraging significant advances in its foundational capabilities and deep model-product co-design, Hy4 unlocks a broader range of real-world productivity scenarios: **Office Productivity & Collaboration**: Hy4 has significantly enhanced the user experience on Tencent WorkBuddy. Evaluation benchmarks show an average performance score of 83.18 and a pass rate of 96.15 percent, with Hy4 ranking first place in nine out of twelve scenarios within the mainland Chinese market. In practical use, Hy4 balances efficiency and effectiveness for visual creative tasks, 3D scene construction, and web development. Furthermore, it delivers marked improvements in document presentation, stability, and usability for human-AI collaborative tasks on WorkBuddy. Leveraging enhanced in-context learning capabilities, Hy4 excels at understanding complex information from diverse sources. Integrated with WeCom via WorkBuddy, Hy4 connects with daily workflow data across chats, emails, documents, calendars, and meetings. When managing multiple projects simultaneously, Hy4 automatically tracks project history and recent developments. It identifies outstanding tasks, flags upcoming meetings that require preparation, and monitors approaching deadlines, helping users prioritize effectively and stay aligned on important follow-ups. In addition, new team collaboration capabilities powered by Hy4 will be introduced with the upcoming release of WorkBuddy’s “Projects” feature. Hy4 has also been optimized for professional financial analysis. By training on thousands of specialized workspaces and tens of thousands of high-quality tasks derived from real-world scenarios, the model gains a deep understanding of expert workflows in fund research, securities analysis, and quantitative investment strategies. In a rigorous blind evaluation conducted by the Tencent Hy team in partnership with Tencent Financial Technology, Hy4 emerged as the top-performing open-source model. The assessment involved 213 financial professionals, including 153 experts from leading external institutions, approximately 70 percent of whom possessed more than five years of industry experience. LLMs.content: [PYMNTS Intelligence](https://www.pymnts.com/pymnts-intelligence/)[The Prompt Economy](https://www.pymnts.com/the-prompt-economy/)[Newswire](https://www.pymnts.com/newswire-announcements/)[Events](https://www.pymnts.com/events/)[SUBSCRIBE](https://www.pymnts.com/subscribe/)[Partner With PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/partnerships/) [About](https://www.pymnts.com/about/)[Contact](https://www.pymnts.com/contact-us/) [![PYMNTS.com home page](/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/PYMNTS_2023_logo_white.svg?v=1.1)](https://www.pymnts.com/ "PYMNTS.com home page") # Tencent Targets Financial Analysis With Hy4 AI Model By [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/author/pymnts/ "Posts by PYMNTS")  |  November 4, 2026 | ![Tencent](https://www.pymnts.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Tencent.jpeg?w=620) [Tencent](https://www.tencent.com/) has released its latest generation large language model, [Hy4](https://hy.tencent.ai/research/hy4), saying in a Wednesday (Nov. 4) [press release](https://www.tencent.com/tencent-launches-hy4-joining-the-ranks-of-the-worlds-leading-open-source-ai-models/) that it “now ranks among the world’s leading open-source AI models.” Hy4 introduces visual understanding capabilities for the first time; introduces computer-use capabilities for the first time; provides major improvements in instruction following, long-context comprehension and long-horizon agentic tasks; and delivers stronger performance across diverse application, according to the release. The new capabilities unlock new opportunities for real-world productivity, the release said. Tencent highlighted office productivity and collaboration, frontend and game development and scientific research. “Hy4 has also been optimized for professional financial analysis,” Tencent said in the release. “By training on thousands of specialized workspaces and tens of thousands of high-quality tasks derived from real-world scenarios, the model gains a deep understanding of expert workflows in fund research, securities analysis and quantitative investment strategies.” Tencent also highlighted cybersecurity and biosafety safeguards the company built into Hy4. The model is trained on defensive security data but not on offensive materials related to exploitation, the release said. In terms of biosafety, Hy4’s capabilities in experimental design are limited in comparison to frontier models, per the release. Tencent will soon release a Hy4 Flash model that is designed for greater cost-efficiency and high-value applications, according to the release. It was reported Wednesday that [Oracle](https://www.oracle.com/) terminated a $7 billion agreement to provide advanced AI [computing capacity](https://www.pymnts.com/cpi-posts/oracle-pulls-out-of-7-billion-tencent-ai-agreement-after-us-pushback/) to Tencent, after U.S. government officials raised concerns about this arrangement with the Chinese company. The proposed five-year contract would have allowed Tencent to use sophisticated AI processors housed in Oracle-operated data centers across Southeast Asia and would have provided Tencent with access to about 100,000 advanced AI chips that are difficult to obtain within mainland China because of restrictions imposed by Washington and Beijing. AI Product.content: Israeli startup Explorium shuts down after raising more than $127 million Founded in 2017 by Omer Har, Or Tamir and Maor Shlomo, who later left the company to focus on Base44, Explorium built a data enrichment platform before pivoting toward generative AI and tools for AI agents. Its founders say it continued to grow over the past year but could not turn that momentum into a sustainable business. The Israeli startup Explorium is shutting down after nearly nine years of operation. Founders Omer Har and Or Tamir announced the closure in a farewell post, describing the company’s efforts to adapt to rapid changes in the artificial intelligence market. Founded in 2017, Explorium raised more than $127 million from investors including Insight Partners, Oren Zeev’s Zeev Ventures, Emerge, F2 Capital and 01 Advisors. Another co-founder, Maor Shlomo, has since gone on to found Base44, acquired by Wix. Explorium was established by Shlomo, Tamir and Har. The company initially developed a data enrichment platform that connected organizations to thousands of external data sources and signals, allowing them to supplement their internal datasets. The aim was to help data professionals improve machine learning predictions and make better business decisions. Applications included predicting customer churn, assessing credit risk and identifying new business opportunities. The company enjoyed considerable success in its early fundraising rounds. In September 2019, it raised $15.5 million in a Series A round led by Zeev Ventures, following a $3.6 million seed round. In July 2020, it secured $31 million in a Series B round, followed by a $75 million Series C round led by Insight Partners in May 2021. The latest financing brought its total funding to more than $127 million. At the time, Explorium employed approximately 130 people and was expanding its operations in Israel and the United States. But the market in which Explorium operated was changing rapidly. As machine learning became increasingly commoditized and capabilities once reserved for specialized providers became more widely available, the company entered a period of change and restructuring. In their farewell post, Har and Tamir said that after Har took over as CEO, Explorium decided to pivot early toward generative AI. Their premise was that AI agents would emerge as a new category of business users, requiring broad access to high-quality data. Building on its existing infrastructure and partnerships, Explorium launched AgentSource in early 2025, describing it as the first B2B data platform designed for go-to-market agents. The product was aimed at a new wave of companies and platforms developing automated sales and marketing tools. The company subsequently introduced what it described as the first B2B data enrichment solution based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). That product evolved into Vibe Prospecting, which the founders called the first standalone in-chat prospecting application. It allowed users to access B2B data and identify potential customers through an AI chat interface. According to the founders, the product attracted more than 350,000 registered users. Despite its efforts to reposition the company for the emerging AI-agent market, Explorium was unable to sustain its operations. Har and Tamir said the company had continued to grow over the past year, even as the market underwent significant upheaval, but that growth ultimately proved insufficient. “Today we are sharing hard news. After almost nine years, Explorium is ceasing operations,” the founders wrote. “We started Explorium believing in the power of AI for business, and that AI is only as good as the data behind it.” They described the company's evolution from data enrichment to products designed for AI agents, before acknowledging that its efforts had not been enough to keep the business going. “Thanks to an extraordinary team, we moved rapidly in a market undergoing real turmoil and kept growing this past year. They fail because nobody finds them. There are over 14,200 active AI tools competing for attention right now. The market is not sitting around waiting to discover yours. If you build something real, ship it quietly to three directories, and wait for users, you will wait a long time. Discovery in 2026 has to be engineered deliberately, across multiple surfaces, on a timeline that runs from 30 days before launch to 90 days after. This guide is the strategic map. How to prepare, when to launch, where to launch, and what to do after the launch-day spike fades so you build traction that actually compounds. ### The failure pattern worth understanding first The numbers are sobering. Research from CIO found that 88% of AI product attempts never reach production traction at all. S&P Global found the average organization scraps 46% of its AI proofs-of-concept before they ship. One analysis tracking more than 319 failed AI startups found that 40% shut down within 24 months. The causes are almost never technical. The pattern repeats: founders build in isolation, skip real user validation, and launch with positioning so vague that a potential user cannot tell within five seconds whether the product is for them. That leads to the single most important idea in this guide. A launch is not a marketing event you bolt on after building. It is the first real test of whether your positioning works, whether your ideal customer is real, and whether the value you built actually lands. The prep work below is how you find that out before launch day, not after. ### Pre-launch: the 30 days that decide everything Most failed launches are decided weeks before the launch date arrives. Everything here happens before you pick a day. ****Write your one-sentence positioning first****. This is the highest-leverage task in the entire process, and most founders rush it. If a stranger cannot understand what your product does in one sentence, your launch posts will confuse people no matter how good the product is underneath. The test is simple. Show your one sentence to someone who does not know you or yourproduct. If they cannot immediately tell who it is for and what problem it solves, rewrite it. Do not launch until it passes. The template that works: “[Product] helps [specific customer] [solve specific problem] without [the current frustrating alternative].” Not “AI-powered [category].” Specific enough that the right person reads it and thinks “that is exactly what I need,” and the wrong person rules themselves out. Positioning that passes this test multiplies across every channel you use. Positioning that fails it undermines every channel at once. ****Validate with real usage****, not opinions. Get 10 people who match your actual customer profile to complete a real task with a rough version of your product. Not a scripted demo. A real goal they actually have. “That is a good idea” tells you nothing. Someone trying and failing to do something tells you almost everything. The product is available as a plugin for ChatGPT and is also integrated with Claude, Databricks Genie, Gemini for business and Microsoft Copilot. Support for Amazon Quick, IBM and Snowflake is expected later. Adobe is pitching the software at marketing teams that want to manage customer journeys, campaign planning and performance analysis from within the AI tools they already use. It is designed to let users plan, orchestrate and adjust customer experience work without switching between multiple applications. CX Enterprise Coworker is part of Adobe's broader customer experience software portfolio and is intended to cover the full customer lifecycle, from prospect acquisition and engagement to conversion and customer lifetime value. The announcement reflects a broader industry push to embed specialist enterprise software into general-purpose AI assistants. Rather than requiring staff to log into separate products, software groups are trying to place business functions directly into the conversational interfaces used across office work. Adobe said the tool is built on open standards including Model Context Protocol and Agent2Agent, which allow it to operate across different AI platforms and enterprise systems while keeping human oversight in place. **AI capabilities** According to Adobe, the product can analyse campaign data, identify trends, forecast audiences, adjust customer journeys and help resolve workflow conflicts. It is also intended to support planning, project management and work management tasks for marketing teams. A second part of the rollout involves new connectors for CX Enterprise Coworker. These pre-built integrations with partner systems let users pull data and trigger actions across several tools through a single request. Among the partner integrations Adobe named are Amazon Ads, Databricks Genie, Demandbase, Meta campaign tools, Microsoft Work IQ, RainFocus and Snowflake Cortex AI. The aim is to reduce the need for customers to carry out custom integration work. That matters because one of the main barriers to AI adoption in large organisations has been fragmented data and workflows. Marketing teams often keep campaign, customer and content information in separate systems, making it harder to coordinate decisions in one place. The purchase price was not disclosed. Founded in 2024, Conductor has offered a service that orchestrates several coding agents simultaneously using models from OpenAI and Anthropic. Meta, which launched its own coding agent Muse Code in August, now adds a multi-agent development environment through the deal. Conductor has stopped accepting new sign-ups and will shut down its cloud service on the 20th, while the local version will be supported into early next year. On the same day, OpenAI also announced plans to acquire a developer-tools startup, underscoring intensifying competition in coding tools. ##### Key Elements ![Meta Acquires AI Coding Startup Conductor, Securing Development Environment for 'Agent Legions'](https://img.biggo.com/4heKWpNJZ_hSz0D5tNugWaSYrj_Em_WwDAvXPfAG4Vc/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTExL2U1ZDhjZWM4LTE1OWEtNGFlOC05YzBiLTkzNWNjNWNkNTg3NV8xNzkzODQzNTcxX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Meta has acquired Conductor, a startup whose platform lets developers run multiple AI agents simultaneously to build software. The move is seen as an effort to expand its presence in the AI-powered development tools market by absorbing outside technology and talent, following the launch of its own coding agent. Conductor said on its website on the 4th (local time) that it is joining Meta. The acquisition price and detailed terms were not disclosed. Founded in 2024, the company launched its core service in July of last year. Its premise is to let developers run multiple AI agents at once, each in its own independent workspace, and carry out software projects in parallel. Agents can be used on cloud, personal computers and mobile devices. Rather than developing its own models, the company pulls in models from major AI companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. This allows developers to operate multiple agents at once while separating tasks within a project and tracking progress. For Meta, the deal secures a touchpoint to draw coding-focused users into its own model ecosystem. The transaction comes as Meta widens its stride in coding. In August, Meta launched Muse Code, its own coding agent for handling large-scale codebases, entering the software development automation business. It has also been pouring money into AI agent-related acquisitions. In March it bought Moltbook, an AI agent social networking service (SNS) platform, and its recently launched Muse agent service was reported to have surpassed 10 million downloads in the United States within 40 days of launch. Industry observers expect the acquisition to let Meta extend its technical capabilities into multi-agent operating environments. However, Meta has not yet laid out specific plans for how it will integrate Conductor's technology into its AI products. As a result of the acquisition, Conductor is winding down its service in stages. The company blocked new sign-ups and app downloads starting the same day, while allowing paying users to keep using the service at no additional charge. The operation runs on two main tracks: theft of [LLM API credentials](https://socradar.io/resources/report/ai-identity-exposure-report-2026.html) from misconfigured cloud infrastructure, and an academic fraud campaign targeting 20 institutions, 19 of them in the US. This exposed tools, scripts, logs and Telegram bot tokens, including tokens for the actor’s own AI agent bots. They look for publicly exposed endpoints or valid LLM API keys. In one case, a script called the `/api/create` endpoint to register models on exposed Ollama servers. Usage chart showing LLMJacking generating a spike in API requests (Source: Google) Sysdig also [documented an exposed Ollama server](https://cyberpress.org/remote-tools-bypass-detection/?amp=1) acting as the reasoning engine for an autonomous penetration-testing framework. Ollama has no native authentication, and port 11434 should never be exposed to the internet. The dominant entry vector was stolen or exposed cloud identity tokens. These included IAM credentials, Service Account keys, GitHub Personal Access Tokens (PATs), and live session tokens. UNC6993 abused a misconfigured Service Account key. It also hosted a fake application portal that told users to paste raw JSON containing an active access token, which bypassed passwords and multifactor authentication (MFA). Another actor used cloud federation tokens to mint fresh access keys and sidestep MFA. FortiGuard Labs described a similar chain in which a [leaked AWS IAM key was used to hijack Amazon Bedrock](https://cyberpress.org/hackers-abuse-leaked-aws-iam-keys/?amp=1) models. According to the [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3373227/tencent-unveils-hy4-open-weight-ai-race-deepseek-zai-alibaba-heats), the release lands as the open-weight race between Tencent, DeepSeek, Z.ai and Alibaba gets more crowded. The Hy4 preview is a 770 billion parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that activates 49 billion parameters per token and ships under the Apache License 2.0. That combination matters to engineers for a plain reason. A permissive license plus downloadable weights means a team can run, fine-tune and ship the model without asking Tencent for permission. Few models at this scale come with terms that clean. This analysis separates what Tencent has confirmed from what circulates in headlines. It covers the architecture, the access channels, the related Hy4 Flash model and the competitive picture. Readers tracking the broader field can compare it with our earlier look at [Alibaba’s Qwen4 plans and the doubts around them](https://shattered.io/qwen4-launch-alibaba-open-source-promise-doubt-470-models-2026/), and with the wider [AI and machine learning coverage](https://shattered.io/ai-machine-learning/) on this site. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. The official wording describes a [large language model](https://shattered.io/category/ai-machine-learning/) built on a Mixture-of-Experts design, with visual understanding as one of its headline abilities. One caveat shapes the whole story. The phrase about joining the ranks of the leading open-source models is a characterization from Tencent and from the headline. The retrieved sources do not establish a precise ranking, and they publish no benchmark table that places Hy4 at a specific position. Infra & Chips.titleZh: Supermicro will sell SambaNova’s inference chips alongside Nvidia GPUs
Infra & Chips.content: Supermicro will build and sell AI inference systems that pair SambaNova’s SN50 chips with Nvidia GPUs, the companies said on Tuesday. The collaboration initially plans for 10,000 SN50 chips, according to SambaNova’s announcement. The racks will join Supermicro’s Data Center Building Block Solutions, the ready-made data centre systems it sells to customers. Running an AI model has two stages. First the system reads the prompt, then it writes the answer piece by piece. In the new racks, Nvidia GPUs do the reading and SN50 chips do the writing, SambaNova said. The company says AI agents work nonstop, so how fast they act depends on how fast the model responds. > “Agentic AI is the next wave of inference, and it has to run everywhere,” said Rodrigo Liang, co-founder and chief executive of SambaNova. “Now customers can order SN50 RDUs alongside GPUs, from a world-leading partner they trust.” ## Who does what Supermicro will put the systems together, test them, deliver them and support customers, including with on-site service. SambaNova engineers will get AI models running and tuned on SN50 and help with deployments. The companies will start with neoclouds, the cloud providers built for AI, and with sovereign clouds. Those keep data and computing inside one country. They then plan to sell to companies that run AI in their own data centres. > “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers,” said Charles Liang, president and chief executive of Supermicro. ## Built for existing data centres SN50 is SambaNova’s fifth-generation Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit, or RDU, a chip designed for inference. The company says it can serve the largest models without needing extreme power density in each rack. A SambaRack SN50 draws an average of 20 kW, SambaNova said last week. Operators can add inference capacity in data centres they already run, according to SambaNova. They do not have to wait for new builds held back by power and cooling. It says they can also keep using their existing GPUs for longer. The two companies say they can deliver much more inference capacity in 2027 as a result. ## SambaNova’s other recent deals The Supermicro deal follows another one with Oracle. Oracle said at its AI World conference on 27 October that it plans to deploy SN50 chips in its cloud data centres. It will offer the capacity to AI model builders. (Photo: THE ELEC) AMD will partner with FuriosaAI and MangoBoost to build a heterogeneous artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure cluster in Seoul next year. Keith Strier, AMD's senior vice president of global AI markets, announced the plan at the AMD Advancing AI Seoul 2026 event held at the Westin Seoul Parnas in Samseong-dong on Nov. 4. "We will sign a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with FuriosaAI and MangoBoost shortly," he said. The company began mass production of its second-generation RNGD in January this year. FuriosaAI claims the chip delivers 1.7 to 1.8 times the performance of Nvidia's H100 at the same power consumption. It has signed a technology validation agreement with LG AI Research and supplied chips to Upstage. MangoBoost's DPU is called BoostX. The chip handles communications, storage input/output and security processing in AI infrastructure. These tasks have traditionally consumed CPU computing resources. By offloading them to a DPU, CPUs can focus on their primary computing workloads. BoostX accelerates GPU communications and storage using standard Ethernet technology. Integrating AMD hardware with Korean-made semiconductors was among the initiatives included in an MOU signed by AMD and South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT at the AI Summit in San Francisco in July this year. The two sides agreed to jointly develop and demonstrate heterogeneous AI computing infrastructure combining AMD chips with Korean AI NPUs. AMD CEO Lisa Su further detailed the initiative during her visit to South Korea in October. She pledged to develop the infrastructure into a reference model for use in global markets. AMD also announced plans to establish an AI Center of Excellence (CoE) with the Ministry of Science and ICT. Election results in Texas and Ohio point to stricter review of AI infrastructure projects. ![](https://f1.tokenpost.com/2024/11/9vga9k0r6d.png) By **[Enna Lee](/reporters/24)** Published ![Sealed hardware crates sit inside an unfinished data-center structure / TokenPost.ai](https://mzwrodgsdjfdyvnraeya.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-media/articles/a87e2bc03c5773435da4ede19ec0b6af040861714ea06daef5eda6dc48f2f044.webp) Sealed hardware crates sit inside an unfinished data-center structure / TokenPost.ai Nvidia shares rose Wednesday, Nov. 4, as recent upbeat results from leading chip companies suggested that concerns about data-center construction delays had not yet affected Nvidia and other hardware firms, even as U.S. election results pointed to stricter project review. Customers continued stockpiling AI hardware despite uncertainty over where suitable installation sites would be available. Recent positive results from leading chip companies suggested construction delays had not immediately affected Nvidia or other hardware makers. Republican governors in Texas and Ohio lost their elections, meaning AI infrastructure projects will face stricter review. Nvidia would face a greater challenge if Democratic officials pursue strict limits on data-center construction. Infra & Chips.content: # SambaNova partners with Supermicro for SN50 RDU deployments Server maker will initially purchase 10,000 SN50 chips from SambaNova SambaNova has partnered with Supermicro for the deployment of SN50 RDU chips. In a statement, SambaNova said Supermicro would initially purchase 10,000 SN50 RDUs from the AI chip company in order to build and sell AI disaggregated inference systems. Those Supermicro systems will comprise both Nvidia GPUs and SambaNova RDUs, with the server maker set to integrate, test, deliver, and support the systems for customers, including providing on-site service. Meanwhile, engineers from SambaNova will ensure AI models are tuned to run on the SN50 chips, and will support Supermicro with deployments, starting with neoclouds and sovereign cloud providers, before expanding to enterprises looking to run AI in their own data centers. SambaNova first unveiled the chips, dubbed SN50 AI, in February 2026, stating that the hardware had been designed to support agentic AI workloads. At the time, the company claimed the RDUs were 5x faster than “competitive chips,” offering a 3x lower total cost of ownership, although it did not name the comparative hardware. Built using the company’s Reconfigurable Data Unit (RDU) architecture, SN50 features a three-tier memory design that supports ten-trillion-parameter models and can power “thousands of simultaneous AI sessions with consistent high performance.” SambaNova added that the chip also offers 4x more network bandwidth than its previous generation, and up to 256 accelerators can be linked over a multi-terabyte-per-second interconnect. "Agentic AI is the next wave of inference, and it has to run everywhere," said Rodrigo Liang, co-founder and CEO of SambaNova. "Supermicro builds AI infrastructure for data centers globally. Now customers can order SN50 RDUs alongside GPUs, from a world-leading partner they trust. That's how fast, efficient inference gets to scale." Charles Liang, president and CEO of Supermicro, added: “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers. Our collaboration with SambaNova expands our broad DCBBS portfolio by enabling heterogeneous architectures that integrate GPU computing with specialized inference acceleration, helping customers deploy efficient, scalable AI solutions.” Founded in 2017, SambaNova previously focused on training workloads, but pivoted in 2025 to become an AI cloud services provider. Its Suite product is touted as an on-prem or cloud-based offering that allows companies to train their own generative AI models based on popular foundation models. The company first unveiled its SambaNova Cloud in September 2024. It provides cloud-based AI inference services using the company’s SN40L AI chip, launched in September 2023 and capable of running models with up to five trillion parameters.

Infra & Chips.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Nvidia Vera CPU: 1.8x Claim vs AMD’s 2.24x Rebuttal [2026] ![Marcus Bell](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/mbell.webp) [Marcus Bell](https://shattered.io/author/mbell/) Updated Nov 5, 2026 · 16 min read Nvidia’s Vera CPU stopped being a roadmap slide on October 27, 2026. That day Nvidia and Oracle said Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin NVL72 systems were generally available on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), which gives server buyers something they can actually rent. The question that follows is blunt: does the NVIDIA Vera CPU beat AMD’s new EPYC Venice processors, or does the speed advantage only exist in vendor slides? Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang framed the OCI launch as a production step. “We are bringing Vera into production on OCI to support these workloads at scale,” Huang said in [Nvidia’s October 27 announcement](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-oracle-expand-nvidia-vera-rubin-to-multi-gigawatt-scale-and-bring-nvidia-vera-cpu-to-oracle-cloud-infrastructure). OpenAI was among the customers with early access on the platform, according to the same release. Both chipmakers now publish numbers that point in opposite directions. Nvidia says its Olympus cores deliver 1.8x faster single-threaded performance. AMD says its own tests show 1.2x the per-core performance and 2.24x the platform-level performance of a Vera-based platform. Neither company has published a price, and the independent data is thin. Cloud specialists such as [CoreWeave, with its NVIDIA Vera CPU rollout](https://shattered.io/coreweave-nvidia-vera-cpu-ai-agents-2026/), will generate the first real-world evidence. For now, the contest between the claims is the story. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Nvidia Vera CPU Goes Live on Oracle Cloud The October 27 announcement bundled three things. Vera CPUs became generally available on OCI. Vera Rubin NVL72, the rack-scale system that pairs Vera CPUs with Rubin GPUs, became generally available on OCI too. And Oracle committed to expanding its Vera Rubin superclusters to multi-gigawatt scale, a plan rather than delivered capacity. One more item sat in the announcement as a plan: HGX Rubin NVL8, an x86-based server with eight Rubin GPUs connected through NVLink. Oracle described it as a configuration it intends to introduce. No shipping date or price accompanies it, so treat it as roadmap. Earlier in the fall, on October 21 and 22, Nvidia said Vera Rubin was in full production and that partners were shipping systems to AI labs, cloud providers and hyperscalers. Our earlier report on [Vera Rubin NVL72 reaching full production and going live on Oracle Cloud](https://shattered.io/nvidia-vera-rubin-nvl72-full-production-2026/) covers the GPU side of that launch. The CPU is where AMD and Intel have the most room to argue, so it gets the focus here. There is a caution built into the record. Nvidia’s materials say Vera Rubin systems ship to cloud providers and hyperscalers, but the sources reviewed here do not confirm shipments provider by provider. Oracle is the clearest named deployment. AWS, Microsoft and the smaller GPU clouds have not been confirmed as receiving commercial Vera CPU shipments in the material available on November 5, 2026. ## Inside the Vera CPU: 88 Cores and a Memory-First Design Nvidia built Vera as a host processor for AI factories, not as a general-purpose chip chasing every x86 workload. The company unveiled it on May 31, 2026 as the host CPU for standalone Vera servers, Vera Rubin systems and BlueField-4 STX storage platforms. Its pitch centers on the CPU jobs that surround a model: tool calls, orchestration and sandboxed code execution for AI agents. ### Olympus Cores ...
